surface: A Practice Brief On Camera: The Scene, Where It Turns And What It Asks
where: Player Profile, Genres, Open Its Brief beside a genre, and the list beside the brief’s title where a genre has two: the line under the title, The Scene (Where And When, The Two Of You, You Play, The Reader Plays, What You Want, What’s In The Way), Where It Turns, and What <Title> Asks with its reasons
why: Read in order on the built pane at 1440 and 390 (nine camera briefs) and as strings for all 205: each sets out a situation an actor can play from its facts alone, a person, a place, what’s at stake and a clock, in the scene’s own words and never the game’s, and each What It Asks reason says why that feature matters in this scene (“Every line races the falling shutter, so each beat has to land to the second.”). Prop and set notes speak to the actor and keep everything on their side of the frame. Every “in the Nth beat” a field names points at the beat it means (checks/beat-references.txt). Found: six second situations in second-b.ts said “on her own side of frame” where every other brief says “on her side of the frame” (14 times), “on his side of the frame” or, to the actor, “on your side of the frame” (33); The Dispensary Door named its door “a flat”, a set-builder’s word nothing in the game explains and that a self-tape at home doesn’t have; The Warm Walls’ arc ended on “then her face shown”, which needs a second reading to find the respirator in it; One More Friday kept the passive “the accent is played as”, which its first-situation sibling Not Going Back and the glossary had replaced.
changes: second-b.ts: “on her own side of frame” → “on her side of the frame” in The Second Fitting, Tuesday Night All Night, Seven Minutes Fast, The Boxes In The Hall, The Approved Lesson and The Warm Walls; The Dispensary Door, “with your back to the barricaded door, a flat on your side of the frame” → “with your back to the barricaded door (a wall on your side of the frame will do)”; The Warm Walls’ arc, “then her face shown as she asks him to leave with her” → “then the respirator off as she asks him to leave with her”. second-c.ts, One More Friday: “…among them, and the accent is played as the way Jean talks” → “…among them. Play the accent as the way Jean talks”, as Not Going Back says it.

evidence.ref: tests/material-words.test.ts: 'shows every brief’s scene, its reasons and its readings whole, each sentence sound'

surface: A Practice Brief With A Staged Fight, A Replica Weapon, A Stunt Or Staged Intimacy
where: The same pane: the beat that holds the contact under Where It Turns, and the staging note under Techniques It Asks (Stage Combat, Intimacy, Clown And Mask) in What <Title> Asks
why: Each of the 34 says its contact once, as an instruction to the actor in the glossary’s safety words: mark it solo at reduced speed against the reader’s called cues from off camera, with no contact; a replica never pointed at the lens or the reader; an embrace agreed in advance with an intimacy coordinator and played to his eyeline beside the lens; a fall worked out slowly onto a soft mat; and how it repeats safely on every take. Read on the built pane (The Loading Bay, The Second Key, The Steward Of The Cellar, at 1440 and 390): the beat says what the body does in the story (“his arm goes wide off frame and the keys drop at her feet”) and the note says how a solo tape stages it, so the drama and the safety never blur. Eyeline, called cues, marking and staged intimacy are the industry’s words, kept as brief 17 asks; each note carries their sense in the words around them (“beside the lens”, “at reduced speed”), and no guide chapter or How This Works entry defines them, which is reported for the tutorial editor.

surface: An Improvised Or Open Practice Brief: Freedom To Improvise And It Only Takes
where: The same pane: Freedom To Improvise and It Only Takes: Open (or Set) under What <Title> Asks, and How You’ll Play It below, where a way the brief doesn’t take says Doesn’t fit
why: Each says what is written and what you find as you tape (fixed points, an outline, the first words of each reply), and each It Only Takes note names the one way the scene can be played with its reason, which the material-words test holds to the brief’s own allows. Read on the built pane (Night Two At Juniper Creek, The Tape For Later, No Meteors Tonight, Out The Door By Seven, at 1440 and 390). Found: three second situations said the take did the work, “leaves every word to the take, the way the form is made”, “leaves the talk to the take”, “You find the last things after it on the take”: the engine’s word standing in for the actor, and in The Tape For Later a “form” the sentence never named.
changes: second-a.ts, Out The Door By Seven: “You find the last things after it on the take” → “Each “last thing” after it is yours to find as you tape”, and its techniques line’s “the last things found on the take” → “the last things you find as you tape”. second-c.ts, The Tape For Later: “leaves every word to the take, the way the form is made” → “leaves every word to you as you tape, the way found footage is made”, as its first-situation sibling says it; No Meteors Tonight: “leaves the talk to the take” → “leaves the talk to you”, and its It Only Takes note’s “With the talk left to the take” → “With the talk left to you”. The engine-speak count of “a take, for any judged work” falls by five.

surface: A Voice Brief: You Speak To, And How It’s Recorded
where: The same pane for a brief recorded alone at a microphone: the line under the title, Where And When’s closing sentence, You Speak To in place of The Reader Plays, and the voice-over line under Techniques It Asks
why: Each of the 36 says once that you record it alone at a microphone (to finished picture, before the animation exists, or for an audio drama), names under You Speak To who is spoken to and how to play to them, and ends with “There’s no reader.” where no one is opposite; a dub glosses itself (“every line must land on the lip movements already in it”). Read on the built pane (Last Launch From The Roof, Notes From The Overnight Bus, at 1440 and 390). Found: Notes From The Overnight Bus closed its circumstances on “He records alone at a microphone.”, which gave the character a microphone on a night bus, where the other 35 tell the actor how the scene is made.
changes: second-d.ts, Notes From The Overnight Bus: “He records alone at a microphone.” → “You record it alone at a microphone, as the voice notes he leaves on his phone.”, as Everything In Order says it of its phone statement.

surface: A Practice Brief’s Readings: Your Reading, It Rests On, And The Reading Named Again
where: The same pane: Your Reading, each reading with its label, its sentence and It rests on; the toast “Reading it as <label>.”; the Reading column of Your Takes Of It and The Last Take
why: Each reading is one sentence of what the scene is, played that way, and an It rests on line that is a fact of the brief above it, so a player can check the reading against the scene without the game’s word for it; none is called right, as the pane’s footnote promises. The labels are short Title Case names (“Talking Him Down”, “The Floor Gives Way”) that read as well again in the Reading column and the toast. Read on the built pane for eighteen briefs at 1440 and 390 and as strings for all of them; every reading that names a beat by number points at the beat it means (23 references, checks/beat-references.txt). A reading id two briefs of one file share is one source in the inventory (Owning Up sits with Brave For Her), which is the tool’s grouping, not a defect on screen.

surface: A Class Scene From A Play, On Its Coursework Card And At The Table Work
where: School, Coursework, a piece set from a scene: the card’s opening sentence (play, author or translator, year, place, the parts), the summary, and the Table Work’s questions with each answer, and once the piece is shown, Why the text supports it or doesn’t under each; and the notice when the piece is set (“Your scene is from …”)
why: Read on the built app’s Coursework tab in the walk of brief 16 as merged (Othello, The Impostures of Scapin, Arms and the Man, King Lear, at 1440 and 390, and Scapin again on the rebuilt app) and as strings for all 46: the summary says what happens in the scene in the play’s own facts, each Table Work answer is a choice an actor could make, and each reason quotes the translation it names exactly, said as the game’s sentence around the quotation. Found: Scapin’s and the mechanicals’ places carried a colon of their own, so the card’s sentence ran “a street in Naples: the sack: you play Scapin”; Scapin’s reason for “Friends who wish each other well” said “Aside, Scapin tells him”, which contradicts itself, an aside being told to no one; Richard III’s reason for “Win her, here, over the body” said he means to marry Warwick’s youngest daughter without saying that she is Anne, so it supports the answer only for a player who knows the history.
changes: scenes-scored.ts, Scapin: place “Act Three, Scene Two, a street in Naples: the sack” → “Act Three, Scene Two, the sack scene, in a street in Naples”; “Aside, Scapin tells him “you shall pay me for that lie.”” → “Aside, Scapin says “you shall pay me for that lie.””. scenes-house.ts, A Midsummer Night’s Dream: “Act Five, Scene One, the palace of Theseus: the mechanicals’ play” → “Act Five, Scene One, the mechanicals’ play at the palace of Theseus”. scenes-classical.ts, Richard III: “He means to marry Warwick’s youngest daughter, and she goes wearing his ring.” → “He means to marry Warwick’s youngest daughter, Anne herself, and she goes wearing his ring.”

evidence.ref: tests/material-words.test.ts: 'shows every scene’s summary and each answer’s reason once it’s shown, and a cut-against reason is the note’s'

surface: A Table Work Answer The Text Doesn’t Support, Said In The Teacher’s Note
where: The simulated note on a shown scene piece (the notice and the card’s feedback) where the note is the choice: “<question>: you answered “<answer>,” but the text doesn’t support it. <reason> You played <part> in <play>.” The template is the coordinator’s (systems/coursework.ts); the reason is this area’s
why: Every unsupported answer’s reason is read after the answer it now names (brief 15’s school change), and the material-words test holds each to that exact sentence for both parts of every scene. Read in that order: the reasons that open “That’s the fourth act; …” now follow the answer they mean, and each says what’s true in its second clause. The one that didn’t hold in the note was Scapin’s “Aside, Scapin tells him”, changed above.
changes: scenes-scored.ts, Scapin: “Aside, Scapin tells him “you shall pay me for that lie.”” → “Aside, Scapin says “you shall pay me for that lie.””, the reason the note gives for “Friends who wish each other well”.
